paper_metadata.title: Discontinuous Precipitation in Ni-Base Superalloys During Solution Heat Treatment

evidence.quote: Discontinuous precipitation in single-crystal Ni-base superalloys during solution heat treatment has been studied.

The test bars for thein situ experiments corresponded to those that were fully solutioned and primary aged.

Cylindrical test bars (70 mm in length with a 10 mm diameter) were cast in an industrial directional solidification furnace. The basic parameters included the following: furnace heater temperature was nominally 1773 K (1500 °C), vacuum level of the furnace chamber was maintained at 0.1 Pa (10–6 atm), and a mold withdrawal rate of around 5 × 10-5 ms –1.

parameters.cooling_method: gas fan quenching with forced Ar flow (~240 K min^-1)

other.isothermal_holds: numerous isothermal holds along ramp to final soak temperature

evidence.quote: The solution heat treatment cycle consisted of numerous isothermal holds along the ramp cycle up to the final soak temperature of 1636 K (1363 °C). The test bars were positioned on ceramic tiles within the center of the furnace working volume and held at 1636 K (1363 °C) for 25 hours.

parameters.cooling_method: rapid gas fan quenching with Ar

evidence.quote: The test bars underwent primary aging in the same furnace at 1423 K (1150 °C) for 5 hours under a vacuum level of 0.1 Pa (10–6 atm) and subsequently rapidly gas fan quenched using Ar.

parameters.cooling_method: quenching in Ar flow (~90 K min^-1)

evidence.quote: Heating involved a series of ramps and isothermal holds until the set temperature was attained and a soak of 0.5 hour at top temperature was used. In this case, a set temperature of 1563 K (1290 °C) was used. After completion of the top soak phase quenching was done in an argon flow at approximately 90 K min –1.
In one instance, a sample was heated up to 1633 K (1360 °C) and then isothermally held for 1 hour before quenching.

An initial ramp rate of by 10 K min–1 was followed by an intermediate isothermal hold at 1523 K (1250 °C) for 90 minutes to allow the furnace temperature to equilibrate. This was then followed by ramping at 5 K min–1 until the final temperature was attained. A final top soak temperature of 1623 K (1350 °C) was used and this was followed by an isothermal hold for 14 hours.
For cooling rates used in industrial practise the as-cast microstructure comprises c dendrites and non-equilibrium inter-dendritic phase.

attributes.location: outer layer beneath surface, thickness ~5 µm

evidence.quote: Nucleation of b-islands occurs beneath the surface and constitutes the outer layer with a thickness ~5 lm. The composition determined by EDS gives Ni Al ¼ 58 36 atomic ratio and indicates that the outer layer corresponds to b phase.

attributes.composition: Ni-Al atomic ratio 74:15; Co = 2.5, Cr = 0.75, [Ta+W+Re] = 6.75 at.%

evidence.quote: c¢ layer with refractory-rich (TCP) phases having ‘‘criss-cross’’ morphology with thickness ~5 lm. The composition measured by EDS yields Ni Al ¼ 74 15 atomic ratio, indicating c¢ phase. The remaining atomic percent is Co = 2.5, Cr = 0.75, [Ta + W + Re] = 6.75.

attributes.location: within discontinuous precipitation zone in gamma prime matrix

evidence.quote: Discontinuous precipitation morphology, comprising of refractory (W and Re)-rich (TCP) phases with a typical needle-like morphology [unlike in (ii)] within a c¢ matrix.
The sample surface is demarcated by the occurrence of an intermittent Al 2O3 layer.
Above the surface, there is the presence of a b-condensate layer, which most likely forms during cooling and this fact is further corroborated by the polycrystalline random orientation of the grains
There is the occurrence of a ‘‘bright’’ phase that is nearly continuous across the surface, which is enriched in refractory elements.

attributes.location: sporadic regions at surface beneath Re/W surface precipitates

evidence.quote: the ‘‘grey phase’’ that occurs sporadically, c.f. point (c) is clearly denuded in Al. However, since this layer is distinctly ‘‘bright’’ compared to c¢ in back-scattered mode, it must be enriched in refractory elements, which in this case should be Ta

attributes.morphology: coarse globular ahead of DP zone; regular cube-type in bulk
attributes.location: DP zone matrix and substrate ahead of DP interface

evidence.quote: The coarse c¢ morphology ahead of the DP zone extends to ~150 lm beyond the DP cell interface into the substrate and the c¢ morphology is roughly globular in shape.

attributes.location: gamma/gamma prime morphology in homogenized alloy

evidence.quote: c (c-channels within c/c¢ morphology in homogenized alloy): Ni Al ¼ 26:24 and Al Ta ¼ 7:17

attributes.location: gamma channel ahead of DP interface

evidence.quote: Also, ‘‘ﬂecks’’ are observed within the c-channel [Figure 8(b)] and these constitute ‘‘secondary’’ c¢ that have precipitated within the channel.

attributes.morphology: colony of gamma prime with needle-like TCP phases

evidence.quote: The DP zone comprises solely of [ c¢ + TCP (needle-like morphology)] and the thickness of this zone is ~20 lm.
The entire surface morphology is polycrystalline.
Growth of the DP zone also occurs into the substrate. Ingress of the zone at the end of the 1623 K (1350 °C) isothermal hold is ~120 lm.

attributes.morphology: coarse islands interspersed between usual gamma/gamma prime morphology

evidence.quote: The substrate beneath the DP zone shows the distinct presence of coarse c¢ precipitates (islands) interspersed between the usual c/c¢ morphology. This was markedly absent in the early stages of DP.

attributes.morphology: irregular gamma/gamma prime, roughly globular coarse gamma prime ahead of DP

evidence.quote: there is an irregular c/c¢ morphology in the region of interest ahead of the DP cell.
Diﬀusion of Al ahead of the boundary leads to gamma prime precipitation and is accompanied by a loss in the driving force available for advancement of the grain boundary.
The driving force calculated for the initial stages of DP was [10-5 to 10-4] N/[ lm2 of the grain boundary].
Discontinuous precipitation (DP) refers to an abrupt change in composition and orientation between parent phase and product phases.
It is found that discontinuous precipitation occurs at temperatures approaching the solvus, where volume diﬀusion is dominant.

mechanisms.name: solute partitioning at growing precipitate tips

evidence.quote: The advancement of the DP zone occurs by partitioning of Cr, W, and Re to the growing tips of the precipitates along the grain boundary.

Depletion of W and Re from the bulk matrix leading to precipitation and growth of TCP phases results in a loss of solid-solution hardening associated with these alloying elements and therefore a concomitant decrease in creep strength.
Through a novel experiment we also demonstrate the response of a grain boundary to remnant strain when all chemical driving force has been consumed, i.e. the occurrence of grain boundary pinning.
